newsitem.title: USA: Prudential to pay Massachusetts $2.4 million. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Prudential to pay Massachusetts $2.4 million. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]

text.p: Massachusetts officials on Thursday said they reached an agreement in principle for Prudential Insurance Co of America to pay $2.4 million to settle claims that the company used deceptive sales practices to sell life insurance.

In addition to refunds to customers, the settlement calls for the payment of $1.2 million to the state attorney general's office for monitoring the settlement process and $1.2 million in fines to the Division of Insurance.
Massachusetts had opposed Prudential's earler settlement agreements, along with Florida, Texas and California.
Florida and Texas earlier Thursday also agreed to similar settlements, leaving California the lone holdout on Prudential's settlement offers.

Under a class-action settlement reached in September, Prudential agreed to pay at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million people who bought permanent life insurance between 1982 and 1995. (Corrects from "between 1982 and 1985.")
That agreement improved the terms of an earlier settlement reached by a multistate task force of insurance regulators that imposed a $35 million fine on Prudential and a restitution program.
A hearing to determine the fairness of the class-action settlement is scheduled for Monday in U.S. District Court in Newark, N.J.
